key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform, reducing grain-boundary barriers and yielding larger, faster-stabilizing photovoltage under illumination.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface passivation can improve carrier landscape stability and potentially reduce photovoltage losses in perovskite solar cells.
method: Illumination- and wavelength-dependent surface photovoltage (SPV) analysis
evidence_signal: The abstract reports CPD distribution narrowing from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, SPV increasing from about 345 to 417 mV, and the stabilization time constant decreasing from about 840 to 470 s after AEAPTMS treatment.
watch_item: The findings are based on thin-film nanoscale surface measurements, so translation to full device performance and long-term stability still needs direct validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
